title: Tofu scramble
summary: Soft, golden curds of crumbled firm tofu with turmeric, nutritional yeast and kala namak for an egg-like flavour, folded with wilted spinach; vegan as written.

ingredients.note: one block, drained and patted dry

steps: Press the tofu between paper towels under a heavy plate for 10 minutes, then crumble it by hand into uneven pieces from pea- to thumbnail-size; irregular curds look most like scrambled egg.
Stir the turmeric and nutritional yeast into the almond milk to make a smooth yellow paste.
Heat the olive oil in a 25 cm (10 in) non-stick skillet over medium heat. Cook the onion 3–4 minutes until soft and translucent, then add the garlic for 30 seconds.
Add the tofu and cook 4–5 minutes, turning occasionally, until the moisture has steamed off and a few edges are lightly golden.
Pour in the yellow paste and fold until every curd is evenly coloured, about 1 minute. Add the spinach and fold until just wilted, 1–2 minutes; the pan should look moist but not wet.
Off the heat, sprinkle over the kala namak and pepper, fold once, taste, and serve at once scattered with chives.
tips: Add the kala namak off the heat: its sulphurous, egg-like aroma fades with cooking. It is salty, so add no other salt until you have tasted.
Unlike egg, tofu does not set or go rubbery if overcooked, but it does dry out; the splash of almond milk keeps the curds soft, so add another spoonful if they look dry.
It reheats well, which scrambled eggs do not, so it can be made ahead for the week.

origin.history: Scrambled tofu was popularised in the United States by vegetarian cookbooks of the 1970s, among them those from The Farm, a commune in Summertown, Tennessee, that published widely read soy-food recipes. No single inventor is known, and similar crumbled-tofu dishes were cooked in East Asia long before. Turmeric for colour and nutritional yeast for savouriness became the standard seasonings; kala namak, an Indian sulphur salt, was adopted later to imitate the taste of egg.
